candidates.tagline: "Finally U vs J" — boxing's biggest fight, ruined by typography
candidates.story: The official promotional poster for the long-awaited Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight accidentally reads 'finally U vs J' due to vertical placement of the fighters' shortened names, drawing F-grade mockery from graphic designers worldwide.
candidates.why_funny: The most hyped boxing match announcement of 2026 shipped a promotional poster that doesn't actually name the right fighters — just whoever 'U' and 'J' are.
candidates.alt: Promotional boxing poster with 'FINALLY' in large bold text and the fighters' names arranged vertically so they read as 'U vs J' instead of Fury vs AJ

candidates.tagline: Apple, the anti-ad company, added a permanent unskippable ad to iPhone Settings
candidates.story: Apple began embedding persistent promotional banners in the iPhone Settings app in iOS that cannot be dismissed, with a red notification badge making sales pitches for iCloud+ indistinguishable from urgent security warnings — even for users already subscribed.
candidates.why_funny: Apple built its brand on mocking Google's ad-driven model, then added undismissable ads disguised as security alerts to the most 'trusted' screen on its own phone.
candidates.alt: iPhone Settings app showing a persistent promotional banner with a red notification badge pushing iCloud+ subscription upgrades
